verdicts.reason: Primary stress falls on look, which contradicts the pronunciation note ("The stress is on up") and the house particle-stress practice for phrasal verbs.
The line lists an old friend under "finding something", but that item is the visit sense, so the sentence muddles the senses.
The example "looked his number up in her phone" falls under this sense, but the definition names only a computer.
The definition uses look for, the verb the learner_errors note says is a different meaning, which invites confusion.
"the times" reads as the newspaper; the typical phrase is "look up the train times" or "look up a time".
Look for is a confusable verb, not a synonym of this sense, and the null note leaves the learner without the difference.

verdicts.quote: I looked for the word in the dictionary.
verdicts.reason: This sentence is grammatical; look for means searching, so it is not an error and the "incorrect" label is false.
